feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform roles: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by useful scale indicators. It reads clearly overall, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce polish.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support a leadership profile in digital platforms, governance, and communications.  
- Good credibility signals: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact and specificity.  
- Broad but coherent scope: web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, AI search, and multimedia are presented as an integrated leadership portfolio.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “digital strategy,” “governance,” “workflows,” and “communications operations” appear frequently across summary, competencies, and roles. Tightening this would improve impact.  
- Fix style consistency: “Coleman DAVIS” is visually inconsistent; choose normal capitalization unless intentional. Also standardize punctuation/list style around bullets and hyphenation (e.g., “organization wide” should be “organization-wide”).  
- Strengthen writing precision: a few phrases are generic (“helping scale,” “strengthened,” “improving decision-making”). Add more outcomes where possible. Minor grammar/style issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is not very relevant and can be removed.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several competency areas listed elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the service list to 3–4 themes rather than 5–6 parallel items.
- Consider rewrite: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, analytics and editorial operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads digital governance, CMS transformation, multimedia production and AI-enabled content experiences, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is echoed across skills sections, so avoid listing too many capability categories in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and aligned to the strongest recent leadership-level capabilities.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-oriented wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems.”
- Prioritize most marketable recent strengths and reduce overlap with other sections: “AI-enabled search and content discovery,” “Workflow automation and platform integrations,” “Public-sector advocacy communications.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure; avoid mixing “systems,” “operations,” and “experiences” inconsistently.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled…experiences” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; consider using fewer, broader categories here.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope will make the footer feel more distinctive and high-impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use a cleaner list format with one concise line per project; drop “Designed/Built/Developed” repetition by varying verbs.
- Add one concrete result, audience, or scale detail where possible, especially for AI Hybrid Search and the microsite.
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently, and spell out “10 x 20-foot” for formatting consistency.
- Consider sharper wording: “bill-level AI chat” → “bill-specific AI chat”; “continued campaign growth” → “future campaign expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and the advocacy video series substantially overlap with current and NACo roles in Work Experience.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; keep it if you want this section to add new information rather than restate prior bullets.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS

items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten it around highest-impact consulting outcomes and make the freelance scope feel more concrete.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into 3–4 outcome-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign and storytelling experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance for coordinated cross-channel communications.
- Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time reduced, engagement gains, search success improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite details duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics language overlaps with the NACo Director role; emphasize what is new/current here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were tighter and each bullet emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, deliverability, production volume, or campaign results if available; otherwise shorten to avoid a generic scope bullet.
- Strengthen results language in later bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/video operations overlap with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same accomplishment verbatim elsewhere.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more as responsibilities than outcomes. Tighten it to emphasize scope, team coordination, and the specific channels/programs you expanded before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show progression and impact: “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing prior to promotion to Director of Digital Media.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague workflow language with a clearer systems angle: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency across digital output.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s “governance” and “planning systems”; keep this version more execution-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the earlier NACo role and footer project list; avoid repeating “built first” claims here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong theme alignment with the candidate’s recent leadership roles, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen seniority and public-sector relevance while using tighter, less repetitive phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use “communications” instead of “messaging” to sound more senior and consistent with the CV.
- Change “audience-focused content planning” to “audience-centered content strategy” for stronger strategic positioning.
- Keep this section purely strategic; leave executional/platform terms to the technical and analytics skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with recent NACo bullets; avoid repeating channel-management language elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. It should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and implementation strengths rather than repeat a software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters tied to recent work: “Drupal platform delivery,” “CMS modernization,” “front-end implementation,” “API and workflow integration,” “AI-enabled search.”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce low-signal items; suggested rewrite:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery
- CMS modernization and migration
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- Airtable-based content and operations systems
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless central to target roles; they read as secondary versus recent Drupal-led work.
- If space allows, use one outcome-oriented phrase such as “enterprise web modernization” instead of generic “technical execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats multiple items already listed in “Technical + IT,” especially platforms and coding languages.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep it in only one prominent skills section if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics leadership and decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Put the highest-value, recent strengths first: KPI design, executive reporting, analytics strategy, then tools.
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper business value.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier such as “decision-ready reporting” or “insight-driven optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave the full tool stack to Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; consider “SEO and UX performance analysis” if you want clearer distinction.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and higher-value production capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Studio, Livestream & Hybrid Event Production”
- Tighten content to: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual production workflows”
- If accurate, add scale/outcome language instead of generic terms, e.g., “In-house studio buildout,” “multi-camera livestream delivery,” or “recurring advocacy video production”
- Keep only 4 items max; use parallel noun phrases and avoid broad terms like “video production and editing” if tools already appear elsewhere

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; rephrase here to focus on studio/event execution
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the NACo bullet about building an in-house studio, so avoid repeating that exact wording unless adding specificity

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s very generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” As a standalone item, it should either add proficiency/context or be merged to avoid wasting space.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put the most relevant platform first and add brief context only where it reinforces recent impact, especially Drupal.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages.”
- If space is tight, cut GitHub Pages unless it reflects meaningful recent use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus related capabilities.
- Consider merging both into one stronger section: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • CMS modernization.”

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and current by emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • jQuery • API and third-party integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value.
- If accurate, add one outcome-linked qualifier in adjacent experience instead of here, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “workflow automation” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider keeping the detailed tools here and shortening the Topline Skills version to avoid repetition.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more selective and frame tools by function to reinforce recent systems/operations leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group and trim for relevance: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Drop older/lower-value items unless central to target roles: Basecamp, Trello
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Workflow automation and team operations: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Slack/Teams are collaboration tools, not automation tools alone; the current heading is slightly misleading.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength in email operations shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise-scale email/engagement capability, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise newsletter operations • Audience segmentation • Journey/campaign setup**
- If accurate, add one qualifier tied to recent scope: **Supported email programs reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders** or **Used for high-volume member communications and newsletter operations**
- Keep platform names first, then 2–3 capability keywords; avoid turning this into a long skills sentence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; keep this item tool-focused and save audience scale/impact for recent roles.
- “Engagement” may also overlap with Core Competencies’ multi-channel communications; use this section to emphasize systems/platforms only.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analytics infrastructure and optimization methods most relevant to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization
- Replace with: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting
- Swap “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “performance analysis” to keep this tools/methods list concrete.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “executive dashboards” for a clearer business outcome.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one section or making this one strictly tools while the Topline section stays outcome-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating all of them elsewhere unless this section is kept very concise.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify outputs or scope so it reads as the foundation for your later leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating: “Mentored a digital media associate and helped standardize day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestream and weekly video content, and improved cross-channel publishing processes.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/early production rather than expansion.
- “Strengthening workflows” also appears in later NACo entries; specify what changed or save broader workflow language for more senior roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes/ownership, while avoiding overlap with later multimedia and digital-content roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production coordination, and rollout.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholder reach, or programs supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item lighter and more innovation/program-focused.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here unless it was a distinct achievement.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads like a mixed list of software and capabilities and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Tighten it into named tools only, or rename it to reflect both tools and production capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Creative Tools & Production” if you want to keep workflows/capabilities in the line.
- Use parallel phrasing and group by type: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast recording/editing”
- If space is tight, keep only software here and let experience entries prove production skills: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
